Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Wed, Nov 4 7:31am to 6:20pm; Thu, Nov 5 7:33am to 6:19pm; Fri, Nov 6 7:34am to 6:17pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Wed, Nov 4 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow is holding. Pam Rocks reads N 18 gusting 23 at 6am, up from 16 at 5am and ahead of the page's 14. Pemberton is still 3 hPa above Vancouver, and Environment Canada's 4am update keeps northerly 15 to 25 easing near noon.

Porteau is a maybe from first light at 7:32 to about 10:30. Low tide is 6.7ft at 8:05, then it floods to 15ft by 3pm, which can flatten the swell. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go. Under 20, stay home. Squamish is an outflow, so skip it.

Thursday afternoon the southeast fills in hard, 25 to 35 in the Strait.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 10:30 AM PCT 04 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Thursday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 15 to 25 knots diminishing to light near noon then increasing to southerly inflow 20 to 30 early Thursday morning.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 10:30 AM PCT 04 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Thursday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind southeast 5 to 15 knots except southeast 15 to 25 near Vancouver Island early this evening and southwest 15 south of Tsawwassen Thursday morning. Wind becoming southeast 15 to 20 Thursday afternoon.
